about: Plain-language summary of what the agent has learned about each person's tastes. Shown and editable under Settings on the calendar. When a person edits their summary, the agent treats every statement in it as correct and keeps it.

aaron.summary:
What I'm working from:
- Big yes: repertory and revival film — noir, Hitchcock, Lynch, character actors, sad and humane stories (you flagged the Kore-eda After Life revival).
- Electronic, experimental and ambient music and DJ nights at artist-run spaces (Junglist Heights, Halloween ATP at Current Space, John Berndt's night at the Red Room).
- Adventurous jazz in small rooms; DIY electronics and synths; photography and small galleries.
- Less likely: arena pop and tribute acts, kids-only programming, sports, pub crawls.

From your flags (29 Interested, none Not interested yet):
- History is still your strongest thread: Doors Open, haunted-houses Profs & Pints, the BMI social night, the Clipper Mill Art & Industry tour.
- Art and exhibitions moved up: you flagged the BMA's two-centuries-of-Baltimore-photography show, MICA's Globe Poster show, and The Stars, the immersive LED light-and-sound piece at The Voxel.
- Talks keep landing — another Profs & Pints (How to Feel Worthy) and André Carrington's Audiofuturism talk — so Guilford Hall's talk series ranks higher.
- Gardening and nature: the Cylburn late-fall gardener's workshop joins Filbert Street Garden and Mushroom City.
- For the Lima trip you flagged the Bioferia de Miraflores farmers' market, so local food markets on trips get a little more room.

What changed since Thursday: six new flags, all Interested — the shift is toward art, design and photography exhibitions, plus local and hands-on things. This refresh added the Red Room's free 32-speaker Wavefield Afternoon (Nov 21), corrected the two DIFFUSION nights at 2640 St. Paul, and added the Jones Falls 2076 closing roundtable at The Peale.
